ANDROID: BACKPORT: partial: mm, oom_reaper: do not mmput synchronously from the oom reaper context (cherry picked from commit ec8d7c14ea14922fe21945b458a75e39f11dd832) Tetsuo has properly noted that mmput slow path might get blocked waiting for another party (e.g. exit_aio waits for an IO). If that happens the oom_reaper would be put out of the way and will not be able to process next oom victim. We should strive for making this context as reliable and independent on other subsystems as much as possible. Introduce mmput_async which will perform the slow path from an async (WQ) context. This will delay the operation but that shouldn't be a problem because the oom_reaper has reclaimed the victim's address space for most cases as much as possible and the remaining context shouldn't bind too much memory anymore. The only exception is when mmap_sem trylock has failed which shouldn't happen too often. The issue is only theoretical but not impossible. Signed-off-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com> Reported-by: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp> Cc: David Rientjes <rientjes@google.com> Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org> Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> Only backports mmput_async. FAFT: Enhance mode_aware_reboot to handle reboot from Recovery mode Previously mode_aware_reboot not handling the post reboot action when rebooting from Recovery mode. If rebooting the device from Recovery in developer mode, mode_aware_reboot didnt bypass the dev screen and need to wait for device to boot into internal device. Now enhancing the mode_aware_reboot to handle the post reboot action when rebooting from Recovery mode. Based on the developer switch position at boot (devsw_boot), we can predict the next boot when rebooting from Recovery mode. If devsw_boot is True, we will call bypass_dev_mode after reboot.
